questions.questionText: An external auditor wants to know exactly who deleted a production Compute Engine instance yesterday. Which specific Google Cloud Audit Log will contain this information?

explanation.general explanation: Admin Activity audit logs contain log entries for API calls or other actions that modify the configuration or metadata of resources. Deleting a Compute Engine instance is an administrative action that modifies resource configuration, so it is recorded here.

why other options are wrong.Data Access audit logs: Data Access logs record API calls that read the configuration or metadata of resources, or read/write user-provided data. They do not record resource deletion.
why other options are wrong.System Event audit logs: System Event logs record Google-initiated actions that modify resources, such as live migration, not user-initiated actions.
why other options are wrong.Policy Denied audit logs: Policy Denied logs record when an API call is blocked by a security policy, such as VPC Service Controls.

questions.questionText: To meet healthcare compliance standards, you need to retain all Google Cloud audit logs for 7 years. You must minimize storage costs, as these logs will likely never be accessed unless explicitly requested during an audit. What is the most cost-effective log routing destination?
options: A Cloud Storage bucket using the Archive storage class
A Cloud Logging custom log bucket
correctAnswers: A Cloud Storage bucket using the Archive storage class

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Storage with the Archive storage class provides the lowest cost for long-term data retention where data is accessed less than once a year. By setting up a Log Router sink to this bucket, you securely and cheaply archive audit logs for 7 years.

why other options are wrong.A BigQuery dataset: BigQuery is excellent for querying logs, but its long-term storage costs are higher than Cloud Storage Archive, making it less cost-effective for pure compliance archiving.
why other options are wrong.A Cloud Pub/Sub topic: Pub/Sub is a real-time messaging service, not a long-term storage repository. Messages typically expire after 7 days.
why other options are wrong.A Cloud Logging custom log bucket: Retaining logs in Cloud Logging for 7 years is significantly more expensive than routing them to a Cloud Storage Archive bucket.

questions.questionText: Your security team requires the ability to perform complex, ad-hoc SQL queries on Cloud Audit Logs to identify irregular access patterns over the last 6 months. Which destination should you configure in your Log Router sink?

explanation.general explanation: BigQuery is Google Cloud's fully managed, serverless enterprise data warehouse. It is the standard destination for exporting Cloud Audit Logs when security teams need to perform fast, complex, and large-scale SQL analysis on log data.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage: Cloud Storage stores raw files (JSON). While you can query it with external tools, BigQuery natively supports high-performance SQL analytics on structured log data.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Pub/Sub: Pub/Sub is used for streaming real-time log events to other systems, not for storing and running historical SQL queries.
why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL is a relational database for transactional applications, not the recommended or native destination for high-volume Log Router sinks.

questions.questionText: A compliance auditor wants to know if any Google engineers or support staff have accessed your project's data while resolving a recent support ticket. Which specific log provides cryptographically verifiable evidence of this activity?

explanation.general explanation: Access Transparency logs provide a record of the actions taken by Google personnel when accessing your Google Cloud content. It includes details such as the support ticket number or business justification, ensuring complete commercial compliance transparency.

why other options are wrong.Admin Activity logs: These log actions taken by *your* users and service accounts that modify resource configurations, not actions taken by Google staff.
why other options are wrong.Data Access logs: These log data-read actions by *your* users, not by Google support personnel.
why other options are wrong.VPC Flow Logs: VPC Flow Logs record network packet metadata, not administrative data access by personnel.

questions.questionText: Your company uses a third-party Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) tool hosted outside of Google Cloud. You need to stream all Admin Activity audit logs to this SIEM in near real-time. What should you configure as the log sink destination?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Pub/Sub is an asynchronous messaging service. By setting a Log Router sink destination to Pub/Sub, you can stream audit logs in near real-time to external tools like Splunk, Datadog, or other third-party SIEM solutions.

why other options are wrong.BigQuery: BigQuery is used for historical SQL analysis, not as a real-time streaming pipeline to an external third-party SIEM.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage: Cloud Storage is used for long-term archiving and batch processing, not real-time event streaming.
why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL is an RDBMS, not a streaming message bus, and is not a native Log Router sink destination.

questions.questionText: A junior administrator notices that they can view Admin Activity logs in the Logs Explorer, but they cannot see logs showing which users ran SQL queries in BigQuery (Data Access logs). Which statement explains this behavior?
options: Data Access logs require the 'Private Logs Viewer' role because they may contain sensitive user data.
Data Access logs must be viewed in the BigQuery console, not the Logs Explorer.
Data Access logs are deleted immediately by default to save storage costs.
Data Access logs are only available to Project Owners.
correctAnswers: Data Access logs require the 'Private Logs Viewer' role because they may contain sensitive user data.

explanation.general explanation: Unlike Admin Activity logs which are visible to the standard 'Logging Viewer', Data Access logs require the 'Private Logs Viewer' (roles/logging.privateLogViewer) role. This is because Data Access logs often contain sensitive information, such as the actual SQL queries executed or data accessed.

why other options are wrong.Data Access logs must be viewed in the B: Data Access logs are viewed in the standard Cloud Logging Logs Explorer, just like other audit logs.
why other options are wrong.Data Access logs are deleted immediately: While they are disabled by default for most services to save costs, once enabled, they are retained for 30 days by default, not deleted immediately.
why other options are wrong.Data Access logs are only available to P: They are available to anyone granted the 'Private Logs Viewer' role; Project Ownership is not required.

questions.questionText: Which two statements are true regarding Cloud Audit Logs in Google Cloud? (Choose two)
options: Admin Activity logs are enabled by default for all services.
Admin Activity logs cannot be disabled by users.
Data Access logs are enabled by default for all services.
Data Access logs are retained for 400 days by default in the _Default bucket.
Admin Activity logs contain the contents of the files uploaded to Cloud Storage.
correctAnswers: Admin Activity logs are enabled by default for all services.
Admin Activity logs cannot be disabled by users.

explanation.general explanation: Admin Activity audit logs are enabled by default across Google Cloud and cannot be disabled by customers. This ensures a persistent, undeniable audit trail of all administrative actions (like deleting VMs or changing IAM policies) is always available.

why other options are wrong.Data Access logs are enabled by default: Data Access logs are disabled by default for most services (except BigQuery) due to the high volume of logs and associated costs.
why other options are wrong.Data Access logs are retained for 400 da: Data Access logs are retained for 30 days by default, whereas Admin Activity logs are retained for 400 days.
why other options are wrong.Admin Activity logs contain the contents: Admin Activity logs record the metadata of actions (e.g., 'Bucket Created'), not the actual payload contents of files.

questions.questionText: Your organization has 50 Google Cloud projects. The compliance team mandates that all audit logs across all projects must be sent to a single, centralized BigQuery dataset in a dedicated 'Security' project. How can you accomplish this efficiently without configuring 50 separate log sinks?
options: Create an aggregated Log Router sink at the Organization or Folder level.
Use a Cloud Function to pull logs from all projects and write them to BigQuery.
Configure VPC Network Peering between all projects and the Security project.
Enable BigQuery Data Transfer Service in the Security project.
correctAnswers: Create an aggregated Log Router sink at the Organization or Folder level.

explanation.general explanation: Aggregated log sinks allow you to capture log entries from an entire Google Cloud organization or folder and route them to a single destination. This completely eliminates the need to manage individual log sinks in each underlying project.

why other options are wrong.Use a Cloud Function to pull logs from a: This introduces massive operational overhead and unreliability compared to the native managed Log Router.
why other options are wrong.Configure VPC Network Peering between al: VPC Peering connects IP networks; it has nothing to do with routing Cloud Audit Logs.
why other options are wrong.Enable BigQuery Data Transfer Service in: BigQuery DTS is used for importing data from SaaS apps and external storage, not for native real-time log routing.

questions.questionText: A compliance framework requires your organization to retain audit logs in a WORM (Write Once, Read Many) compliant storage system for 5 years to guarantee they cannot be tampered with. Which combination of services should you use?
options: Cloud Logging with a 5-year retention period

explanation.general explanation: By routing logs to a Cloud Storage bucket and enabling Bucket Lock with a 5-year retention policy, you ensure that the log files cannot be modified or deleted by anyone (including administrators) until the 5 years expire, satisfying strict WORM compliance requirements.

why other options are wrong.BigQuery with time-travel enabled: Time travel allows recovery of deleted data for up to 7 days, but it does not provide strict, unalterable WORM compliance for 5 years.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Pub/Sub with dead-letter topics: Pub/Sub retains messages for a maximum of 31 days and is not a storage archive.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Logging with a 5-year retention pe: While Cloud Logging can retain data, Cloud Storage Bucket Lock provides the certified WORM compliance layer required by regulators.

questions.questionText: During a routine audit, you notice multiple entries in the 'Policy Denied' audit logs. What do these specific log entries indicate?
options: A Google Cloud service request was blocked by a VPC Service Controls perimeter.
A user entered the wrong password when authenticating to Google Workspace.
A firewall rule dropped an incoming TCP packet.
A Compute Engine VM failed to boot due to an invalid OS image.
correctAnswers: A Google Cloud service request was blocked by a VPC Service Controls perimeter.

explanation.general explanation: Policy Denied audit logs are generated when an API request is denied because it violates a security policy. The most common source of these logs is VPC Service Controls blocking an API request that attempts to cross a secure perimeter.

why other options are wrong.A user entered the wrong password when a: Authentication failures are logged in Cloud Identity / Google Workspace logs, not GCP Policy Denied logs.
why other options are wrong.A firewall rule dropped an incoming TCP: Network packet drops are recorded in VPC Firewall Rules Logging or VPC Flow Logs, not Policy Denied API logs.
why other options are wrong.A Compute Engine VM failed to boot due t: This would appear in serial console logs or Error Reporting, not Policy Denied logs.

questions.questionText: You want to enable Data Access audit logs for Cloud Storage to track who is downloading files. However, you are concerned about the extremely high volume of logs and the resulting storage costs. How can you capture Data Access logs while minimizing costs?
options: Use log exclusion filters in the Log Router to discard unimportant Data Access logs.
Change the format of the logs from JSON to CSV to compress the data.
Enable Data Access logs only on weekends.
Route the logs to Cloud NAT for compression.
correctAnswers: Use log exclusion filters in the Log Router to discard unimportant Data Access logs.

explanation.general explanation: Log Router allows you to create exclusion filters. You can enable Data Access logs for a service, but configure an exclusion filter to discard (not ingest into Cloud Logging) specific, high-volume logs that are not relevant to your compliance audit, saving costs.

why other options are wrong.Change the format of the logs from JSON: Cloud Logging does not allow you to change the fundamental payload structure from JSON to CSV to save ingest costs.
why other options are wrong.Enable Data Access logs only on weekends: This creates gaps in the audit trail, violating compliance rules which require continuous logging.
why other options are wrong.Route the logs to Cloud NAT for compress: Cloud NAT is a networking service for outbound internet access, completely unrelated to log compression.

questions.questionText: A Cloud Architect needs to prove to a compliance auditor that no one can tamper with or delete the organization's central audit logs. Which two configurations should the architect implement to guarantee the integrity of these logs? (Choose two)
options: Create an aggregated Log Sink at the Organization level to route logs to a dedicated Security project.
Apply a Bucket Lock retention policy on the destination Cloud Storage bucket.
Grant the Project Owner role to all developers to ensure visibility.
Store the logs on a standard Compute Engine Persistent Disk.
Export the logs using Cloud Functions to a local text file.
correctAnswers: Create an aggregated Log Sink at the Organization level to route logs to a dedicated Security project.
Apply a Bucket Lock retention policy on the destination Cloud Storage bucket.

explanation.general explanation: To ensure log integrity, you must isolate them. By creating an aggregated sink at the Organization level pointing to a central, heavily locked-down 'Security' project, individual project owners cannot modify the sink. Applying Bucket Lock ensures that even the Security Admins cannot delete or modify the archived logs.

why other options are wrong.Grant the Project Owner role to all deve: This violates least privilege and allows developers to delete the logs, ruining the audit trail.
why other options are wrong.Store the logs on a standard Compute Eng: Persistent Disks are mutable and cannot be strictly locked against tampering like GCS Bucket Lock.
why other options are wrong.Export the logs using Cloud Functions to: This is unmanageable, unscalable, and provides zero cryptographic tamper-evidence.

questions.questionText: Your company uses a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. You need to audit the specific IP addresses and ports that your pods are communicating with over the VPC network. Which logging feature should you enable?

explanation.general explanation: VPC Flow Logs record a sample of network flows sent from and received by VM instances, including GKE nodes and pods (if VPC-native). This provides the IP addresses, ports, and protocols needed to audit network-level communications.

why other options are wrong.Admin Activity audit logs: These record API calls that change resources, not the actual network traffic payload or IP headers.
why other options are wrong.GKE Audit Logs: These log interactions with the Kubernetes API server (like 'kubectl create pod'), not the network packets flowing between pods.
why other options are wrong.Firewall Rules Logging: This logs whether a specific firewall rule allowed or denied traffic, but VPC Flow Logs provide a continuous view of all network connections.

questions.questionText: To meet compliance, your security team needs two distinct log delivery mechanisms: 1) Logs must be retained cheaply for 10 years. 2) Critical IAM policy changes must trigger an immediate alert in an external SIEM. Which two Log Router destinations should you configure?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Storage (using Archive class) is the standard destination for cheap, long-term 10-year log retention. Cloud Pub/Sub is the standard destination for streaming logs in near real-time to trigger immediate alerts in external SIEMs.

why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL is a relational database and is not a supported destination for the Cloud Logging Log Router.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine: GKE is a container orchestration platform, not a log sink destination.
why other options are wrong.Identity-Aware Proxy: IAP secures web applications and does not store or route audit logs.

questions.questionText: Which type of Google Cloud audit log captures actions taken by Google systems on your behalf, such as a Compute Engine live migration or an automated managed instance group scale-up?

explanation.general explanation: System Event audit logs record Google-initiated actions that modify the configuration of your resources. This includes automated infrastructure tasks like a Compute Engine live migration event.

why other options are wrong.Admin Activity audit logs: These record actions initiated by your human users or service accounts, not by automated Google systems.
why other options are wrong.Data Access audit logs: These record user reads of data or metadata, not system events.
why other options are wrong.Access Transparency logs: These record manual actions taken by Google personnel (like support engineers), not automated system background events.

questions.questionText: Your organization is implementing VPC Service Controls. Before enforcing the perimeter and potentially breaking production traffic, you want to audit which API calls would be blocked. What feature should you use?
options: VPC Service Controls Dry Run mode
correctAnswers: VPC Service Controls Dry Run mode

explanation.general explanation: VPC Service Controls offers a Dry Run mode. In this mode, the perimeter logs API requests that violate the policy into the 'Policy Denied' audit logs, but it does not actually block the traffic. This allows you to audit the impact safely before enforcement.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Armor Security Policies: Cloud Armor protects HTTP load balancers from edge attacks; it does not dry-run API perimeter boundaries.
why other options are wrong.IAM Policy Troubleshooter: This tool explains why a user was granted or denied access based on IAM roles, not VPC Service Control network perimeters.
why other options are wrong.VPC Firewall Rules Logging: This logs network-level VM traffic, not API-level perimeter violations.

questions.questionText: You are investigating a security breach where an attacker accessed a Cloud Storage bucket over the weekend. Where can you find a chronological list of API calls showing the IP address of the attacker who downloaded the files?

explanation.general explanation: Downloading files from Cloud Storage is a read operation of user-provided data. This action is recorded in the Data Access audit logs, which capture the caller's identity, IP address, timestamp, and the specific object accessed.

why other options are wrong.Admin Activity audit logs: These log administrative changes (like changing IAM policies or deleting the bucket), not the reading/downloading of data.
why other options are wrong.Security Command Center Findings: SCC might generate an alert if the bucket was public, but the raw chronological list of API download calls is in the Data Access logs.
why other options are wrong.VPC Flow Logs: VPC Flow Logs capture raw network packet metadata, not the application-layer API calls to Cloud Storage.

questions.questionText: You are creating a new Log Router sink to export logs to a Cloud Storage bucket. To adhere to strict security policies, you must ensure that the logs written to this destination bucket are encrypted with a key controlled by your internal security team. What should you configure?
options: Enable Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) on the destination Cloud Storage bucket.
Configure the Log Router to encrypt the logs before exporting.
Use a Customer-Supplied Encryption Key (CSEK) inside the Cloud Logging console.
Encrypt the logs manually using a Cloud Function before they reach the bucket.
correctAnswers: Enable Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) on the destination Cloud Storage bucket.

explanation.general explanation: Log Router relies on the native encryption capabilities of the destination service. By enabling Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) on the destination Cloud Storage bucket, any logs written to it by Cloud Logging are automatically encrypted with your managed key.

why other options are wrong.Configure the Log Router to encrypt the: Log Router does not have an explicit encryption toggle; it relies on the destination bucket's encryption settings.
why other options are wrong.Use a Customer-Supplied Encryption Key (: Cloud Logging does not support CSEK for log sinks. It supports CMEK on the destination bucket or BigQuery dataset.
why other options are wrong.Encrypt the logs manually using a Cloud: This introduces unnecessary complexity and potential data loss when native CMEK on the bucket provides a managed solution.

questions.questionText: Which IAM roles must a user possess to create a new Log Router sink at the project level and view sensitive Data Access logs? (Choose two)

explanation.general explanation: To create or modify a log sink, the user needs the `roles/logging.configWriter` role. To view sensitive Data Access logs (which contain PII or user data), the user needs the `roles/logging.privateLogViewer` role.

why other options are wrong.roles/logging.viewer: This role allows viewing standard logs (like Admin Activity), but explicitly prevents viewing Data Access logs.
why other options are wrong.roles/storage.admin: This manages Cloud Storage buckets, but does not grant permissions to configure Cloud Logging sinks or read logs.
why other options are wrong.roles/compute.networkAdmin: This manages VPCs and firewalls, unrelated to log configurations.

questions.questionText: Your company integrates its on-premises Active Directory with Google Workspace. An auditor wants to verify who changed a user's group membership in the corporate directory. Where would you find these specific identity audit logs?
options: Google Workspace / Cloud Identity Admin console
correctAnswers: Google Workspace / Cloud Identity Admin console

explanation.general explanation: Identity management, group memberships, and directory sync logs are maintained in the Google Workspace or Cloud Identity Admin console. While GCP relies on these identities, the authoritative audit trail for identity changes resides in the Workspace/Cloud Identity audit logs.

why other options are wrong.Google Cloud VPC Flow Logs: These record network traffic, not identity directory changes.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine Serial Console logs: These contain VM boot sequences, not corporate directory logs.
why other options are wrong.Security Command Center: SCC provides threat detection for GCP resources, not audit logs for Google Workspace directory changes.

questions.questionText: A compliance standard requires that every SQL query executed against your BigQuery data warehouse is logged and retained for 1 year. By default, BigQuery query events are written to which log, and do you need to manually enable it?
options: Data Access logs; enabled by default for BigQuery.
Admin Activity logs; disabled by default for BigQuery.
System Event logs; enabled by default for BigQuery.
Data Access logs; disabled by default for BigQuery.
correctAnswers: Data Access logs; enabled by default for BigQuery.

explanation.general explanation: BigQuery is unique among Google Cloud services: its Data Access logs (which record the actual SQL queries and data read events) are enabled by default and cannot be disabled. This ensures a persistent audit trail for data warehousing operations.

why other options are wrong.Admin Activity logs; disabled by default: Admin Activity logs record table creations/deletions, not the SQL queries reading data. Also, Admin logs are always enabled by default.
why other options are wrong.System Event logs; enabled by default fo: System Events record automated Google tasks, not user SQL queries.
why other options are wrong.Data Access logs; disabled by default fo: While Data Access logs are disabled by default for *most* GCP services (like Cloud Storage or Compute Engine), they are uniquely enabled by default for BigQuery.

questions.questionText: You are auditing the security of your Cloud Run deployments. You need to verify if any developers have deployed services allowing unauthenticated public access. Which service can automatically check this configuration against security baselines and flag it?

explanation.general explanation: Security Health Analytics (part of SCC) continuously scans your GCP environment for misconfigurations and compliance violations. It will automatically flag Cloud Run services that allow unauthenticated public access (allUsers), saving you from manually checking each service.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Audit Logs: Audit Logs record when the setting was changed, but SCC is the tool that actively checks current posture against baselines.
why other options are wrong.IAM Policy Troubleshooter: This tool helps debug specific user access denials; it does not scan the whole project for compliance misconfigurations.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Trace: Cloud Trace is a distributed tracing system for application latency, not a security posture scanner.

questions.questionText: A corporate policy states that developers must not be able to bypass auditing by deleting the Cloud Logging sink that exports data to the central security project. What is the most robust way to enforce this?
options: Create the Log Sink at the Folder or Organization level instead of the Project level.
Remove the 'Project Editor' role from all developers.
Use a Cloud Function to automatically recreate the sink if it is deleted.
Store the sink configuration in a Secret Manager vault.
correctAnswers: Create the Log Sink at the Folder or Organization level instead of the Project level.

explanation.general explanation: Sinks created at the Organization or Folder level capture logs from all underlying projects. Because Project-level administrators (like developers) do not have permissions at the Folder or Organization level, they cannot modify, bypass, or delete these aggregated sinks.

why other options are wrong.Remove the 'Project Editor' role from al: Project Owners can still delete project-level sinks. Moving the sink to a higher hierarchy level is the structural solution.
why other options are wrong.Use a Cloud Function to automatically re: This is a brittle, reactive workaround. A Folder-level sink prevents the deletion proactively.
why other options are wrong.Store the sink configuration in a Secret: Secret Manager stores API keys; it does not prevent IAM users from deleting resources in Cloud Logging.

questions.questionText: You need to present evidence to an auditor that Google Cloud is compliant with SOC 2 (Service Organization Control 2). Where can you download the official SOC 2 report for Google Cloud?

explanation.general explanation: The Google Cloud Compliance Reports Manager is a self-service portal where customers can access and download Google's official third-party audit reports and certificates, including SOC 1/2/3, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS.

why other options are wrong.Security Command Center: SCC is for monitoring the security posture of your specific cloud deployment, not downloading Google's corporate audit reports.
why other options are wrong.Google Cloud Console Dashboard: The general dashboard provides billing and resource overviews, not compliance certificates.
why other options are wrong.IAM Recommender: This tool suggests reducing overly permissive roles, completely unrelated to compliance report documents.

questions.questionText: Which two Google Cloud services or features act as sources (producers) of audit logs indicating that a user accessed a virtual machine securely from the internet without a public IP?

explanation.general explanation: When a user accesses a private VM over the internet, they use Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for TCP forwarding, which generates logs verifying the connection. Additionally, OS Login verifies their SSH access and generates logs indicating the user authenticated to the Linux OS.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage Audit Logs: These log bucket/object access, unrelated to VM remote access.
why other options are wrong.Cloud CDN Logs: CDN caches web content globally, unrelated to SSH/RDP access to a VM.
why other options are wrong.VPC Network Peering Logs: Peering connects internal networks, it does not manage or log end-user SSH remote access.

questions.questionText: Your security operations center (SOC) relies on a third-party tool like Splunk. They want to ingest Google Cloud audit logs immediately as they happen. Which integration pattern is the Google Cloud best practice for this architecture?
options: Configure a Log Router sink to a Pub/Sub topic, and have Splunk subscribe to that topic.
Configure a Log Router sink to Cloud Storage, and have Splunk download the files daily.
Configure Splunk to directly query the Cloud Logging API every 5 seconds.
Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service to push logs to Splunk.
correctAnswers: Configure a Log Router sink to a Pub/Sub topic, and have Splunk subscribe to that topic.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Pub/Sub is an asynchronous, scalable messaging service. The best practice for integrating GCP logs with third-party SIEM tools (like Splunk) in near real-time is to sink the logs to a Pub/Sub topic. The external tool then uses a pull subscriber to ingest the stream.

why other options are wrong.Configure a Log Router sink to Cloud Sto: This is a batch process, not real-time, failing the immediate ingestion requirement.
why other options are wrong.Configure Splunk to directly query the C: Polling APIs continuously is inefficient, prone to rate limiting, and does not scale well. Push-based pub/sub is preferred.
why other options are wrong.Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service to pu: BigQuery DTS pulls data *into* BigQuery; it does not push logs out to a SIEM.

questions.questionText: You configured a VPC Firewall rule to block SSH traffic (port 22) from the internet. A developer claims their connection is timing out. You want to audit the firewall to confirm if the rule is actively dropping the developer's packets. What should you enable?

explanation.general explanation: Firewall Rules Logging allows you to audit whether a specific VPC firewall rule allowed or denied traffic. When enabled on the deny rule, you can see a log entry every time a packet from the developer's IP is dropped by that specific rule.

why other options are wrong.Admin Activity audit logs: These log the *creation* or *modification* of the firewall rule itself, not the actual network packets it drops.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Armor Security Policies: Cloud Armor protects HTTP/S load balancers at the edge, not basic VPC TCP firewall rules.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Trace: Cloud Trace tracks application-level request latency, not network-level firewall packet drops.

questions.questionText: You are auditing access to secrets stored in Secret Manager. You need to determine which service account retrieved the database password 10 minutes ago. Which audit log provides this specific payload visibility?
options: Data Access audit logs for Secret Manager
Admin Activity audit logs for Secret Manager
correctAnswers: Data Access audit logs for Secret Manager

explanation.general explanation: Accessing (reading) a secret payload from Secret Manager is considered a data read operation. Therefore, you must look in the Data Access audit logs (specifically the `AccessSecretVersion` API call) to see which identity retrieved the password.

why other options are wrong.Admin Activity audit logs for Secret Man: Admin logs show who created or deleted the secret, not who read the actual sensitive payload value.
why other options are wrong.System Event audit logs: These log automated Google actions, not service accounts retrieving secrets.
why other options are wrong.VPC Flow Logs: These log IP traffic, not the specific API calls to Secret Manager.

questions.questionText: By default, how long does Google Cloud Logging retain Admin Activity audit logs without any custom log bucket configuration?

explanation.general explanation: By default, Google Cloud Logging retains Admin Activity audit logs, System Event audit logs, and Access Transparency logs for 400 days in the `_Default` and `_Required` log buckets. Data Access logs are retained for 30 days.

why other options are wrong.30 days: This is the default retention period for Data Access logs, not Admin Activity logs.
why other options are wrong.7 days: This is not a standard default retention period for audit logs in GCP.
why other options are wrong.Indefinitely: Logs are not kept indefinitely by default; if you need them forever, you must route them to Cloud Storage.

questions.questionText: You are preparing for an ISO 27001 audit. The auditor asks for proof that Google Cloud ensures data is encrypted at rest. What is the fundamental mechanism Google uses to provide default encryption at rest without customer configuration?
options: Google-Managed Encryption Keys automatically encrypt all customer content at rest.
Customers are required to upload a Customer-Supplied Encryption Key (CSEK) for every project.
Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) encrypts the disks before data is stored.
Data at rest is only encrypted if the customer uses Cloud Key Management Service (KMS).
correctAnswers: Google-Managed Encryption Keys automatically encrypt all customer content at rest.

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud employs strong default security. All customer content stored at rest (e.g., in Cloud Storage, Persistent Disks, Cloud SQL) is automatically encrypted using Google-Managed Encryption Keys. This requires zero configuration from the customer and fulfills baseline compliance audits.

why other options are wrong.Customers are required to upload a Custo: CSEK is an advanced, optional feature for customers who cannot let Google hold keys, not a mandatory requirement for baseline encryption.
why other options are wrong.Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) encrypts the: IAP is an access control proxy for web traffic, not a disk encryption tool.
why other options are wrong.Data at rest is only encrypted if the cu: KMS (CMEK) is optional for custom key control. Default encryption happens automatically without KMS interaction by the customer.
